title: os start --home (or -d) organization-ownership refusal prints ceremony commands that name no database, so following them verbatim plans a different database
body:
qa#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUARzLeR7GhKms8a5s

QA-source: #31486 · cli.organization-ownership-ceremony · observed beside the clauses

Found off-clause by the QA run #31486 (subject `0647dabb`) while re-judging #29882, whose fix (the refusal now carries the auth secret) holds only in part.

## Reproduction

1. Copy a v17-shaped SQLite database (a `create-objectstack@17.7.0` blank scaffold, booted once by its own `os dev`) to `H/data/objectstack.db`.
2. In `examples/app-showcase`, with `OS_DATABASE_URL` unset: `os start --no-ui --no-compile --home H -p PORT` → exit 1, printing "Run 'OS_AUTH_SECRET=\"$(cat H/auth-secret)\" os migrate organization-ownership --out PLAN' … then run '… --apply --plan-file PLAN --backup-taken'".
3. Run that plan command verbatim in the same directory → exit 1 "✗ Refused: This database holds none of the platform tables the inventory names (0 table(s) listed), so it is not an ObjectStack database the ceremony can plan — check --database-url / $OS_DATABASE_URL." The served database is unchanged.

Contrast: with `OS_HOME=H` exported for both commands, the plan writes (exit 0). `os start -d file:X` shows the same gap.

## Mechanism

- `os start` resolves its database as `--home` > `$OS_HOME` > the project's `.objectstack`, then `HOME/data/objectstack.db` (`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`, around lines 188 and 286).
- The ceremony defaults to `$OS_DATABASE_URL` or the project database (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`, lines 342–345).
- The refusal sentence (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`, `ceremonyCommand`, line 129) carries the auth secret since #29882 but no `--database-url` (or `OS_HOME`) when start's home or database came from a flag.

## Why it matters

On a tree that also holds a pre-18 project database, the printed commands would plan and apply against that database instead of the one being served.

Owning packages: `@objectstack/runtime` (the boot-guard message) and `@objectstack/cli` (the start hand-off). Full evidence: #31486, slice C1.
